thread:
zoe: Heads up — after today's OIDC client swap some SCIM provisioning actions started failing with KMS errors and a handful of users got unexpected status flips. I rolled back the OIDC client but the provisioner still fails decrypts for tokens created in the 08:12-08:17 window. Logs: 
```
2026-07-08T08:16:42Z scim-provisioner error="InvalidCiphertextException" token=tok-8f3a user=olivia@example.com
2026-07-08T08:16:45Z scim-provisioner http 403 PATCH /Users/789 -> {"error":"forbidden"}
```
Any quick triage ideas? @ops-lead @lia-security

kai: I'm on it. First Qs: which principal is used by the provisioner and did infra-automation touch KMS alias/policy during the OIDC swap? Also, did we change vault/KMS key rotation settings?

zoe: provisioner runs as `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/scim-provisioner`. Deploy shows an `oidc-switch` stage at 08:12:10 and `alias-sync` at 08:13:02 by infra-automation. infra-bot shows PutKeyPolicy at 08:13:05.

infra-bot: [AUDIT] event=PutKeyPolicy user=infra-automation resource=alias/scim-provisioner time=2026-07-08T08:13:05Z change=restrict-external id=pkp-1155

lia-security: check CloudTrail for PutKeyPolicy and for ReEncrypt/GenerateDataKey calls. Also check IAM policy changes for scim-provisioner role around 08:12. Hypothesis: the alias moved or key policy removed the role as an allowed principal.

kai: grabbing policies. Found that alias/scim-provisioner was repointed to a newly created key (pk-3a2b) during alias-sync. Old key (pk-1d2e) still exists but alias now points to new key. Token metadata does not include key-id. That matches InvalidCiphertextException. Also found PutKeyPolicy that added a condition limiting decrypt to principals with `aws:PrincipalTag/role_env=prod`. scim-provisioner didn't have that tag because it's a shared infra role.

ops-lead: mitigation immediate steps: 1) pause alias-sync job, 2) restore alias to old key temporarily so provisioner can decrypt existing tokens, 3) add fallback alias list in provisioner config to try known key aliases, 4) widen SCIM deprov grace to avoid user churn. Zoe please apply 1 and 2.

zoe: paused alias-sync and restored alias to pk-1d2e. Patch applied: `aws kms create-alias --alias-name alias/scim-provisioner --target-key-id pk-1d2e` (recreated alias after verifying key state). Also bumped SCIM grace to 72h via config.

kai: after alias restore I'm seeing successful decrypts for older tokens and 200s on SCIM calls at 08:20:33. Example: 
```
2026-07-08T08:20:33Z scim-provisioner http 200 PATCH /Users/789 user=olivia@example.com action=update
```
But tokens issued after 08:13 were encrypted with pk-3a2b and won't decrypt against the old key; we need a re-encrypt path to consolidate tokens to the new key or preserve both keys via explicit key-id metadata.

lia-security: we should treat alias reuse / repointing as a high-availability hazard. Action items: - require unique alias names per key version (alias/scim-provisioner-v{hex}) - include key-id in token metadata at encrypt time - disallow PutKeyPolicy that adds conditional denies without a documented migration plan and owners - add a CloudTrail alert that pages security when alias is deleted or PutKeyPolicy removes runtime principals.

ops-lead: followups: @kai implement re-encrypt helper and migration script, @zoe run reconciliation for any users changed in the incident window, @lia-security own policy gating + alerting. Also disable alias-sync until infra-automation adds preflight checks. ETA EOD for owner deliverables.

sre-bot: [INCIDENT] service=scim-provisioner incident=INC-2026-0708-11 status=mitigated mitigated_by=zoe mitigated_at=2026-07-08T08:22:19Z runbook=https://redwood.runbooks/internal/scim-provisioning-triage :white_check_mark:

kai: note for vuln triage — automation that touches KMS aliases and key policies should be flagged as high-risk and go through change control. This is both a security and availability vulnerability. I'll draft a short blameless postmortem.

zoe: final status — provisioner healthy, decrypt errors gone for restored tokens, we've queued a re-encrypt job for mixed-key tokens and paused alias-sync. Moving to postmortem. (reactions: :thumbsup: from kai, :eyes: from lia-security)
